title: Count the peaks
objective: count_peaks(heights) should count how many positions are strictly higher than both of their neighbours.
expected: Only inner positions can be peaks. The first and last positions never count. Short or empty lists return 0.
constraints: Do not count plateaus: a value must be strictly greater than both neighbours.

advice.diagnosis: The loop on line 5 runs to the last index, so heights[i + 1] goes past the end of the list and raises an IndexError.
advice.rationale: Stopping the loop one position earlier with range(len(heights) - 1) keeps i + 1 inside the list.
advice.note: Incorrect. It removes the crash, but the loop still starts at 0, where heights[i - 1] wraps around to the last element. A high first value can then be counted as a peak, for example [5, 1, 2] returns 1.

staticWarnings.message: Negative index: when i is 0, heights[i - 1] reads heights[-1], the last element of the list.

prediction.question: After applying the suggested patch, what does count_peaks([5, 1, 2]) return?

suspiciousLineCheck.question: The code checker flagged line 6 of the patch. What happens there when i is 0?
options: heights[i - 1] reads the last element, so the first position can be counted as a peak
Nothing, the loop never uses i = 0
heights[i + 1] goes past the end of the list
suspiciousLineCheck.answer: heights[i - 1] reads the last element, so the first position can be counted as a peak
